bluf: Semetrical is a European search and data consultancy set up by the cofounders of Lumar (formerly Deepcrawl) that now sells itself as AI native: GEO, SEO, analytics and custom AI agents, with its own tools named Tomo, Ogorki5 and Dexter. The record lists no dated move, and its newest case study is dated 2024-03-15. Horus reads it Favored at 29.8 with no headwind listed. What a rival should know: it sells AI visibility while its own site blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended and publishes no llms.txt, and it sells paid search with 0 Google ads of its own.
doing:
The positioning line, "AI-native search and data consultancy helping ambitious brands stay visible in AI-powered search through GEO, SEO, analytics and custom-built AI tools," describes a technical search shop rebuilt around AI answers: visibility in answer engines, classic SEO, analytics and bespoke AI builds. The headline claim, "Set up by the co-founders of Lumar (formerly Deepcrawl), bringing enterprise engineering rigour to AI-era search," sells engineering lineage from crawler software rather than a client roster; the work page adds a claim of "award-winning services" with no award named.

It leads with AI Search / GEO, Data & Measurement and SEO, each scored 3 by the capability read. The GEO page covers indexing audits, brand query testing and AI reporting; the data line rests on Data Insights in the site title, four data services and the OnTheMarket reporting suite; SEO rests on its technical heritage and organic cases for Flexioffices, Equinox Kombucha and FDM. The other core lines score 2: AI Automation / Agents, an AI Consultancy for custom agents and LLM integration with remote MCP servers cited on the about page, and Paid Search, led by the Cloudflare program across 19 markets (+239% conversions). The proprietary tools Tomo, Ogorki5 and Dexter are named without description, and no partner is listed.

The AI posture is the whole pitch: GEO for answer engines, agents and LLM integrations for clients, its own AI tools, and P6 partial for AI operator depth. Its insights feed covers a conversational analytics agent on GA4 BigQuery data and accessibility in the agentic web.

The record lists no dated moves, news, jobs or pricing. The case studies it holds run from 2023-10-16 to 2024-03-15, and none describes GEO or agent work, so the lead line carries no client proof. Also absent: an office, a founding year, a headcount, an owner and any partner.
clients:
The record types the client base as mixed across Property, Technology, Recruitment & training, Food & beverage, Travel and Publishing. No office is listed and the region is Europe, but the excerpts place the work in the UK: Flexioffices as "the UK's number one office brokerage" with "prime London leads", OnTheMarket as "a UK property challenger brand".

In all, thirteen clients are named: twelve observed and one names only. Organic demand leads, on 11 of them. Cloudflare came for paid search across 19 markets, the 2024-03-05 excerpt claiming conversions up 239% and year on year traffic up 650%, coded organic demand and paid performance; it also sits on the transmission and salt-agency books, the one shared client. OnTheMarket appears in case studies on an analytics and reporting suite with a 30% increase in organic CTR (2024-03-15), on PPC traffic and leads, and on hyper local PPC and display with leads up 62% and CPA down 54% (2023-11-21), coded data and measurement plus organic demand. FDM bought integrated SEO and paid media across eight markets (2024-02-28: nonbrand organic up 137%, paid CPA down 51%). JPIMedia came for a migration of 140 websites (2023-10-16), coded organic demand plus web build and platform, and Arkadin for SEO across 38 websites (2023-11-29, nonbrand clicks up 43%). Ocean Florida is names only, a slug reading "ocean florida disney competition". Fish4 and Fish4jobs are counted apart though the Fish4 row borrows the Fish4jobs title, so the pair is likely the same brand; Your Overseas Home and The Craftory have case studies but no client field, outside the count.

Under KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), this organic heavy base will likely need its visibility in AI answers measured and defended, which it sells but has no case study for (moderate confidence).
house: Say and do holds on 1 of 3 tested lines, a house integrity of 33.3. Paid Search is contradicted: its Transparency Center record shows 0 Google ads, and 0 LinkedIn ads match the name query. openings:
The strongest opening is the crawler contradiction. Semetrical sells visibility in AI answer engines while its own site blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended and publishes no llms.txt. A rival that practises AI visibility on its own house and can show its own citations will very likely win any buyer who checks (high confidence, observed). Falsifier: those crawlers admitted and an llms.txt published at the next compile.

Second, the GEO line has no client proof: the case studies on record end at 2024-03-15, none describes AI search work, and no audited AI visibility product shows (P1 partial). A rival with dated AI visibility results for UK brands is likely to win the organic heavy clients that KJ1 puts in play (moderate confidence). Third, it sells paid search with 0 Google ads of its own and no sign of testing ads inside assistants (P8 absent). Cloudflare, also on the transmission and salt-agency books, is a client that shops and a roughly even chance to be contestable. A price attack is a roughly even chance at displacement 59.2, and its onshore claim is thin enough to test in the room.

I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and any pricing below $20 CPM test the KJ2 tailwind, which it does not yet act on (P8 absent).

I1, Comscore monthly AI prompt share, in the Comscore Q3 report expected around December 2026: Gemini at or above 40% or ChatGPT at or below 45% favors S1, while no assistant above 50% with Claude and Perplexity rising favors S2, a reading that bears on KJ3 and on the cost of its crawler blocks.
The record lists no dated move, so the newest case study, 2024-03-15, is the date to beat: a dated GEO case study would change the proof read.
